question: N in SONAR stands for:
solution:
Full form of SONAR is given below-

SONAR = **Sound Navigation and Ranging**

SO → Sound

N → Navigation

A → and

R → Ranging

Here, **N** stands for **Navigation.**

Hence, **Option (4)** is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__Concept - __

__
 
• SONAR: 
 
 
• Sound Navigation And Ranging are what Sonar stands for.
 
• It's a tool for determining the distance, direction, and speed of underwater artifacts such as water hills, valleys, icebergs, submarines, and sunken ships.
 
 
 
• WORKING: 
 
 
• The bottom of a ship is equipped with SONAR, which consists of a transmitter and a receptor or detector.
 
• Ultrasonic waves are generated and transmitted by the transmitter. These waves pass through seawater and are reflected back and received and registered by the detector after hitting objects at the sea's bottom.
 
• The sonar unit calculates the time it takes for ultrasound waves to move from the ship to the seafloor and back.
 
• The time it takes for ultrasound waves to pass from the ship to the seabed is half of this time.
 
• The term "echo-ranging" refers to this method of measuring distance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76983944e7dddb87dd34fab7b3cbda2108fab131f27524bb51c7c8ac801d4990.png] 

 
• WHY ULTRASONIC SOUND WAVES ARE USED: 

 
 
• In the sea, sound waves go further than radar and light waves.
 
• Ultrasonic sound waves (sounds with a frequency greater than 20,000 Hz) are used due to their high frequency and short wavelength with which they can penetrate water over long distances, whereas ordinary sound waves or infrasonic waves cannot.
 
 

Explanation -__

 
• SONAR uses ultrasonic sound waves because of their greater frequency with which they can penetrate deep within the oceanic or seawater to measure distances. 
 
• Hence the SONAR is a device to measure the distance, direction, and speed of underwater objects. It uses - Ultrasonic sound waves.
